notMutated: RoomGeometry.IsCoveredBy's sweep is not mutated as a sweep: every check in RoomBorderDepthTests runs through it, and h1, h2 and c1 change what it is asked or whether it is asked rather than what it answers. Breaking it breaks all of them.

WallBandsInFrontOf reading the row north instead of south (`cell.Y + 1` -> `cell.Y - 1`) is not run separately: no room cell of the shipped map has a wall to the north that paints over a border stroke — the #139/#147 ladder exists to keep the border clear of exactly that band — so the mutant collapses into h2, which is run. Independent review derived the same conclusion by reading.

The manifest's own entries (WorldDrawPass of the four routines) are covered by The_two_halves_of_the_border_are_declared_in_the_two_passes and by the pre-existing WorldDrawPassGuardTests set; w2 is the one recorded here because it is the only one whose failure is not obvious from reading the diff.

corner.finding: Independent review, round 2, F2. Under round one's per-edge decision the outline of quarters@19,2 opened at its bottom-left corner: the south edge of the cell with a wall in front stayed above the depth pass while the west edge meeting it went below and was cut off by that same wall. The opposite corner of the same room, with no wall in front, stayed shut — an asymmetry inside one outline in one frame. Round one's write-up called the change to the vertical edges a correction rather than a price; that wording is withdrawn.
corner.measurement: gap = 8.625 − (inset + 1.0) reference px: the wall's reach above its own footprint, less where the horizontal stroke's upper edge sits. Executable as RoomBorderDepthTests.The_first_round_of_156_opened_the_corner_at_a_wall_in_front (before) and An_outline_closes_at_the_corner_a_wall_in_front_reaches (after), at 32, 40 and 48.
corner.negativeMeansClosed: A negative gap is an overlap: the vertical stroke reaches a half-stroke past the top of the horizontal one, which is what a closed corner looks like.
